items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I think he augmented it with Coleman Hawkins and Henry Red Allen, I believe, and Higginbotham -- and they were not regular members of my orchestra at the time.

ctx.x: Before we go on again to this question of discrimination, another thought occurs to me. Here you are playing in the early 20's, mid 20's, late 20's -- and we're down again now in the early 30's, and all this is New York music; you'd been to Pittsburgh -- Teddy Wilson came from Chicago, what about New Orleans? Do you hear anything about New Orleans at that time? Is New Orleans something known in New York as a particular kind of music, or is New York its own little hotbed and source of music?

Yes and no. New Orleans was certainly known, and the music was very popular; as a matter of fact, Louis Louis Russell came with an orchestra that included Paul Barbarin on drums and Henry 'Red' Allen, both you know, all great New Orleans players. And they raised a pretty good stir in New York, and Jelly Roll General Morton came to New York, if I believe -- he was a New Orleans player, wasn't he?

ctx.x: at that period, could improvise very well, and still didn't know a C from an F diminished you know. That is, by name. They would know it by sound, but not by name, not necessarily.

Just like -- oh, we'll take a reasonably advanced, well ... not reasonably advanced, but a very advanced musician, like Red Allen. Red Allen would run a diminished change against anything, and make it sound good, you know, because he does it with such authority, and you'd say, oh, I know he you meant that ... and you'd start to think of chord substitution, really, you know -- even though the guitar and the piano were doing something else.

Uh huh. What about in this early stage. You know, many musicians, as they describe their development, began by -- I was gonna say 'merely' or 'simply', but that's not really quite the word -- but began by copying note for note, solos of musicians that they admired. And many, many musicians recount how they had done this in the formative stages.
